The preliminary round began on 1 August 2026, followed by the tournament proper on 7 August 2026. This season's EFL Cup final will be held at [[Wembley Stadium]] on Sunday, 21 March 2027, marking the 20th consecutive year that the venue has hosted the competition's final. [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] are the defending champions, having beaten [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[2026 EFL Cup final|previous season's final]].{{cite news |author=Hytner, David |title=Manchester City win Carabao Cup after Nico O'Reilly's double downs lacklustre Arsenal |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/22/arsenal-manchester-city-carabao-cup-final-match-report |work=[[The Guardian]] |publisher=Guardian Media Group |date=22 March 2026 |access-date=19 September 2026}} The winner of the competition qualifies for the play-off round of the [[2027–28 UEFA Conference League]].{{cite web |author=Winterburn, Sarah |title=How Premier League teams qualify for 2027/28 Champions League and Europa competitions |url=https://www.football365.com/news/how-premier-league-teams-qualify-for-2027-28-champions-league-and-europa-competitions |website=[[Football365|Football365.com]] |publisher=Planet Sport Ltd |date=19 September 2026 |access-date=20 September 2026}} ==Teams== All 92 clubs in the Premier League and English Football League entered the season's EFL Cup.{{cite web |title=EFL Cup second round: Premier League clubs' fixtures revealed |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4687523/efl-cup-second-round-premier-league-clubs-fixtures-revealed |publisher=Premier League |date=10 August 2026 |access-date=19 September 2026}} Access was distributed across the top 4 leagues of the [[English football league system]]. There was a preliminary round before the first one due to the number of teams participating in Europe. This round consisted of the two newly promoted sides to [[2026–27 EFL League Two|2026–27 League Two]] – [[York City F.C.|York City]] and [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] – and the two lowest finishers not relegated from [[2025–26 EFL League Two|2025–26 League Two]], [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] and [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]].{{cite web |title=York host Crawley; Tranmere welcome Rochdale in EFL Cup |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/clyp4648pe0o |website=bbc.com |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=3 June 2026 |access-date=4 June 2026}} {| class="wikitable" !Phase{{Cite web |title=Carabao Cup 2026/27 Preliminary Round draw |url=https://efl.com/news/2026/june/03/carabao-cup-2026-27-preliminary-round-draw/ |date=3 June 2026 |access-date=4 June 2026 |publisher=English Football League |language=en}} !Clubs entering in this round !Clubs advancing from previous round !Number of ties !Week commencing |- ![[2026–27 EFL Cup#Preliminary round|Preliminary round]]

(2 clubs) |{{n/a}} | * 2 winners from semi-finals |1 | 21 March 2027 |} ==Rule changes== The regulations governing the EFL Cup were amended ahead of the [[2025–26 EFL Cup|2025–26 season]] to allow, in certain circumstances, a player to represent two clubs during the same season’s competition.{{cite news |last1=Colman |first1=Jonty |last2=Kinsella |first2=Nizaar |title=Chelsea's Guiu eligible for EFL Cup after mix-up |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c89d12091qgo |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=23 September 2025 |access-date=22 September 2026}} Under those provisions, a player who [[Transfer (association football)|transferred]] before the first leg of the semi-final could represent their new club in the [[Two-legged tie|second leg]] and, if selected, the final. A transfer completed after the first leg, however, rendered the player ineligible for any further participation in that season's competition. As a result, they could not feature in the final should their new club reach it. For the 2026–27 season, the regulations have been amended further. A player who transfers during the [[Transfer window|winter transfer window]] is now permitted to appear in the final for their new club, provided they satisfy the other eligibility criteria. They cannot, however, represent one club in the first leg of the semi-final and another in the second. There has also been a modest revision to the regulations concerning [[Loan (sports)#Association football|players on loan]]. From 2026–27, a player registered on loan is automatically eligible to participate in the EFL Cup for their loan club, unless their parent club expressly provides otherwise. Previously, loan players needed written permission from their parent club before they could take part in the competition. ==Preliminary round== The preliminary round was required for the 2026–27 EFL Cup following the participation of nine [[Premier League]] clubs in European competitions, equalling the Premier League record set the previous season.{{cite web |author=Coverdale, David|title=How Palace's UEFA Conference League triumph affects European qualification |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4671711/how-crystal-palace-uefa-conference-league-final-affects-european-qualification |publisher=Premier League |date=27 May 2026 |access-date=20 September 2026}} It featured the two clubs promoted from the [[National League (division)|National League]], York City and Rochdale, and the two clubs that finished 21st and 22nd respectively in the [[2025–26 EFL League Two|previous season's League Two]], Tranmere Rovers and Crawley Town. The round reduced the number of teams entering the subsequent rounds so that 32 clubs could participate in the third round, when the nine European qualifiers entered the competition. The draw was held on 3 June 2026, with Sanny Rudravajhala of Sky Sports hosting and former goalkeeper [[Lee Camp (footballer)|Lee Camp]] performing the draw.{{cite web |author=Johnson, Nick |title=Carabao Cup 2026/27 – Preliminary Draw |url=https://chesterfield-fc.co.uk/news/preliminary-carabao-cup-draw |website=chesterfield-fc.co.uk |publisher=Chesterfield F.C. |date=3 June 2026 |access-date=20 September 2026}} It paired newly promoted [[York City F.C.|York City]] with [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] at the [[York Community Stadium]], while [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] were handed [[home advantage]] against [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]]. Tranmere Rovers and Rochdale contested the opening match of the preliminary round at [[Prenton Park]] on 1 August, drawing 2–2, with Rochdale winning the ensuing [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] 2–1. [[Charlie Whitaker]] and [[Jordan Davies (footballer)|Jordan Davies]] scored for Tranmere, while [[Ryan East]] and [[Zain Silcott-Duberry]] replied for Rochdale.{{cite web |title=Tranmere miss four penalties in cup exit to Rochdale |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce852vq2n1vt |website=bbc.com |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=1 August 2026 |accessdate=20 September 2026}} Rochdale missed their first two penalties but converted their next two, while Tranmere missed four of their attempts in succession after scoring their first, resulting in their elimination. It was only the second EFL Cup meeting between the clubs, following Rochdale's 3–2 aggregate victory in the [[1987–88 Football League Cup#First round|1987–88 first round]].{{cite web |title=Tranmere
